skill.name: team-collaboration-standup-notes
skill.description: Generate clear async standup notes from Git commits, Jira tickets, Obsidian notes, and calendar context for remote teams.
skill.summary: Creates structured daily standup updates from recent work signals and team context.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced examples, and sample commands for the intended standup workflow. One temporary-file handling issue is confirmed, and semantic review found privacy and prompt-injection risks from aggregating workplace data into generated notes.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary file stores aggregated work context.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp, restrictive permissions, and cleanup traps for any generated context file, or avoid writing sensitive context to /tmp.

remediation.issue: Generated notes may expose sensitive source data.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit redaction guidance for customer data, credentials, incident details, private calendar items, and confidential project names.

remediation.issue: External source text is passed into AI prompts without injection guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Treat Jira, Obsidian, calendar, and commit text as untrusted data, and instruct the model to ignore embedded commands from those sources.

remediation.issue: Automation examples include scheduled execution and posting commands.
remediation.suggestion: Keep human approval mandatory before posting and document that scheduled jobs should only create drafts.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Workplace Data Aggregation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow combines Git commits, Jira tickets, Obsidian notes, and calendar events, then can post the generated note to Slack after review. Without redaction rules, generated standups may disclose confidential project, personal schedule, or incident details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines show broad data-source aggregation and an optional Slack posting path. Human approval reduces severity, but the privacy exposure is a real workflow risk.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Source Content In AI Prompt
semantic_findings.description: Jira comments, Obsidian notes, calendar entries, and commit messages are treated as context for AI generation. The prompt does not explicitly tell the model to ignore instructions embedded in those source records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The playbook passes multiple external content sources into an AI generation step. No malicious payload is present in the skill files, but the design lacks prompt-injection handling for source data.

content.value_statement: Remote teams need concise daily updates without adding more meetings. This skill gathers recent work context and turns it into reviewable standup notes.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes recent Git commits into accomplishment bullets.
Connects Jira ticket status to yesterday, today, and blocker sections.
Uses Obsidian daily notes and task completions as context.
Includes calendar events when planning daily availability.
Formats notes for Slack, Obsidian, email, or written standup channels.
Highlights blockers, dependencies, and follow-up owners.
limitations: Requires user-approved access to Git, Jira, Obsidian, and optional calendar tools.
Generated notes may include sensitive project details if inputs are not filtered.
It does not verify ticket accuracy beyond available source data.
Automation examples need local review before use in production workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Daily Engineering Updates
use_cases.description: Turn commits, tickets, and notes into a short standup post before the workday starts.

use_cases.title: Track Distributed Team Progress
use_cases.description: Create consistent async updates across time zones without requiring a live meeting.

use_cases.title: Surface Blockers From Work Signals
use_cases.description: Identify dependencies, delayed tickets, and repeated work patterns that need team attention.

prompt_templates.title: Draft A Basic Standup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request using manually supplied notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise standup note from these bullets. Use Yesterday, Today, and Blockers sections. Keep each bullet short and clear.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Recent Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Use recent commits and task notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my recent commits and completed tasks. Group related work into accomplishments, link tickets when visible, and flag missing context.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Async Team Updates
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a remote team update with priorities.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an async standup note for a distributed team. Include completed work, today priorities, meeting impact, blockers, and specific asks.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Reviewable Automation Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe standup generation workflow using Git, Jira, Obsidian, and calendar inputs. Include permission checks, redaction steps, and human review before posting.

output_examples.input: Recent commits, two completed Jira tickets, and one calendar-heavy afternoon.
output_examples.output: A standup note with completed feature work, two linked ticket updates, limited afternoon capacity, and no blockers.

output_examples.input: Daily notes mention a blocked database migration and an unanswered access request.
output_examples.output: A blocker-focused update that names the dependency, the needed access, the owner to contact, and the escalation plan.

output_examples.input: Several small bug fixes and code reviews across one service.
output_examples.output: A grouped engineering update that combines related fixes, highlights review support, and lists the next validation step.

best_practices: Review generated notes before posting them to any shared channel.
Redact customer names, credentials, incident details, and private calendar information.
Keep updates outcome-focused and include clear owners for blockers.
anti_patterns: Do not auto-post generated notes without human approval.
Do not include raw private notes when a short summary is enough.
Do not turn every commit into a separate standup bullet.

faq.question: Does this skill post updates automatically?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow includes human review before sharing a generated note.

faq.question: Which tools can it use for context?
faq.answer: It can use Git history, Jira tickets, Obsidian notes, and optional calendar data when those tools are available.

faq.question: Can I use it without Jira?
faq.answer: Yes. Jira context is useful, but the skill can still draft notes from commits, notes, and manual input.

faq.question: Is it suitable for async teams?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on clear written updates for teams working across time zones.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Filter source data, redact private details, and approve the final note before posting it.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
